title: Context Bagging: Inference-Time Ensembling for Robust Long-Context QA Under Hard Distractors

contributions.purpose: Allocate test-time compute to context diversity instead of decoding diversity for robust long-context QA.
contributions.mechanism: Context Bagging (CoBag) samples K diverse context subsets via relevance-weighted selection, randomly permutes paragraph order within each subset, generates answers with greedy decoding, and aggregates by majority voting.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on a noisy MuSiQue split with hard distractors, where CoBag significantly outperforms self-consistency.
contributions.source_quote: First, we propose Context Bagging (CoBag), an inference-time method that allocates test-time compute to context diversity rather than decoding diversity for robust long-context QA.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that context-level diversity beats decoding-level diversity under hard distractors.
contributions.mechanism: Head-to-head comparison of CoBag against self-consistency at matched inference budgets on MuSiQue with hard distractors.
contributions.evaluation: CoBag achieves +3.12 EM improvement over self-consistency (p<0.001).
contributions.source_quote: Second, we demonstrate that context-level diversity significantly outperforms decoding-level diversity (self-consistency) under hard distractors, with CoBag achieving +3.12 EM improvement (p<0.001).

contributions.purpose: Isolate which component of context diversity drives the improvement.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation decomposing CoBag into order diversity (paragraph shuffling) and subset diversity (relevance-weighted subset sampling).
contributions.evaluation: Order diversity is the dominant mechanism (+1.44 EM) while subset diversity adds marginal benefit (+0.40 EM), suggesting simple order shuffling may suffice for many applications.
contributions.source_quote: Third, we reveal through ablation that order diversity is the dominant mechanism, suggesting that simple order shuffling may be sufficient for many applications.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work addresses this limitation by introducing context-level diversity rather than relying solely on decoding diversity.
Our approach is most closely related to permutation-based methods but extends beyond order diversity to include subset diversity through relevance-weighted sampling.

Unlike these approaches that ensemble at the retrieval or model level, our method ensembles at the context level by creating diverse views of the same retrieved passages through subset sampling and order shuffling.

notes: Partial self-undermining ablation flagged by the paper itself: the novel subset-diversity component contributes only +0.40 EM while simple order shuffling (+1.44 EM, close to prior permutation self-consistency ideas) is the dominant mechanism. Evaluation is on a single benchmark (noisy MuSiQue split).
